title: Policy Warden: unified evaluation engine and admin gateway for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver 'Policy Warden' — a unified, low-latency policy evaluation engine plus an admin-facing gateway that centralizes RBAC v2 rule authoring, decisioning, and audit emission for API/runtime/console surfaces. Scope includes (1) an evaluation runtime library that can be embedded in the runtime and exposed via a gRPC decision API, (2) an admin gateway component for console interactions, policy snapshots, and SAML/SSO-linked role mappings, and (3) a hardened audit sink that streams canonical audit events (decision, explain, principal-change) to Kafka and BigQuery.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Decision P50 < 1.2ms and P99 < 6ms for typical token counts, measured under synthetic workload (see perf harness).
- End-to-end deny/explain path surfaced in Console with human-readable deny reasons and a single-click evidence link.
- All authorization decisions produce a structured audit event (schema v2) and persist to audit pipeline within 2s.
- SSO/SAML role sync: incoming assertions can be mapped to RBAC groups; tests for idempotent sync and conflict resolution.
- Backwards compatibility: fallback to existing authorizer for policies not yet migrated, controlled by feature flag.

Design notes & trade-offs: 
- We opt for an embeddable evaluator (wasm-ish design) + centralized decision gRPC to reduce cold-path overhead for Console vs full sidecar approach. Trade-off: single-binary embedding increases release coupling but reduces network hops and observability gaps.
- Policy language: convert existing declarative YAML rules to a normalized intermediate form at compile time. This supports faster rule indexing and smaller runtime footprint.
- Caching: implement a TTL'ed decision result cache keyed by (principal, resource, action, policy_snapshot_id). Decision caching reduces cost but must be invalidated on policy or group changes — we will hook cache invalidation into the admin gateway snapshot writer.
- Explainability: include structured deny reasons and top-contributing rules to aid debugging and auditability; this increases event size but is critical for incident triage.

Implementation plan: 
1) Prototype evaluator library with policy compile+index + unit tests (ENG-314160).
2) Build admin gateway REST/GQL surface with snapshot management and SAML mapping editor (ENG-314161).
3) Integrate audit sink and backfill pipeline; wire to telemetry (logs + traces).
4) Canary rollout: 5% of internal traffic -> 25% -> 100%; feature flag per-tenant to opt-in.

Testing & observability: 
- Perf harness at github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-eval/harness (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-eval/pull/42).
- E2E tests exercising SAML assert->role mapping and deny explain path.
- Dashboards: 'RBAC Decisions' (deny_rate, eval_latency_p50/p99, cache_hit_rate, audit_emitted/sec).

Docs & artifacts: 
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Security/Policy+Warden+Design (draft).
- Admin UI mockups: Drive:/redwood/designs/policy-warden-mockups.png.
- Linked PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345, github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/9876.

Rollout & migration: 
- Migration strategy uses snapshot-based rollouts. Initial rollout will be internal tenants + internal infra. For customer-facing tenants we provide a migration window and compatibility mode where requests are forwarded to legacy authorizer on mismatch.

Risks & mitigation: 
- Risk: policy mismatch producing unexpected denies. Mitigation: default permissive canary with auto-rollback, and 'dry-run' flag to log but not enforce.
- Risk: audit volume spikes. Mitigation: adaptive sampling policy and retain full events for 7 days by default, full retention behind opt-in.

Runbook pointers: ensure runbook includes instructions to disable enforcement and to regenerate policy snapshots if corruption suspected. See runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Policy+Warden+Runbook

audit_schema: v2: {event_id, timestamp, principal_id, principal_source, action, resource, policy_snapshot_id, decision, explain: [top_rules], request_id, trace_id}
test_plan: Unit tests for compile/index/decision paths; perf harness tests under synthesized load profiles; integration tests for SAML mapping and dry-run enforcement path; chaos test to simulate policy-store lag and validate cache invalidation semantics.
implementation_notes:
Prefer idiomatic Rust for evaluator core for tight memory control; expose a thin gRPC shim for non-Rust hosts. Ensure public API is stable for 3 minor releases. Use protobuf v3 for decision API. Audit events should be JSONL and validated against schema before sending to Kafka.
Link to perf dashboard: grafana.redwood.local/d/rbac-decision
